subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw core own named, release-tested hosting profiles, and which minimal profile/readiness contract should be accepted first?
rationale: The proposal creates permanent public configuration, health, status, probe, and release-conformance obligations that implementation quality alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept readiness foundation
options.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, requiring separate acceptance and live conformance evidence for each non-local profile.

options.title: Accept all four profiles
options.body: Approve local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode together and own their stable selection, predicate, upgrade, and release-testing guarantees.

options.title: Keep checks host-owned
options.body: Decline core profile selection and continue exposing generic runtime facts for hosts and supervisors to validate externally.

recommendation.title: Accept readiness foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the condition model and default local projection first, requiring separate acceptance and live conformance evidence for each non-local profile.
